headline: Social media giants sued for alleged role in four child deaths
summary: Meta, TikTok, Snap, and Google face a wrongful death lawsuit accusing them of creating addictive platforms that contributed to the deaths of four children.
details: The Social Media Victims Law Center (SMVLC) has filed a personal injury and wrongful death lawsuit against Meta, TikTok, Snap, and Google in Delaware.
The lawsuit alleges that these companies knowingly created addictive and dangerous products, ignoring internal research and concealing evidence of harm.

It claims that the platforms profiled minors during vulnerable moments, pushing content like diet ads and appearance-changing filters, leading to depression, self-harm, and suicidal ideation to boost engagement.
The deaths cited in the lawsuit occurred between July 2024 and September 2025 in Texas, North Carolina, Minnesota, and Tennessee.
Google has responded, stating that providing a safer experience for young people is core to their work and that they are reviewing the claims.
This legal action follows similar lawsuits, including one by four US states against Meta and a settlement by Meta, Snap, and TikTok with a Kentucky school district over social media addiction.
caption:
Four families are suing Meta, TikTok, Snap, and Google, alleging their platforms contributed to the deaths of their children.

The Social Media Victims Law Center (SMVLC) has filed a personal injury and wrongful death lawsuit against Meta, TikTok, Snap, and Google in Delaware.

The lawsuit alleges that these companies knowingly created addictive and dangerous products, ignoring internal research and concealing evidence of harm.

It claims that the platforms profiled minors during vulnerable moments, pushing content like diet ads and appearance-changing filters, leading to depression, self-harm, and suicidal ideation to boost engagement.

The deaths cited in the lawsuit occurred between July 2024 and September 2025 in Texas, North Carolina, Minnesota, and Tennessee.

Google has responded, stating that providing a safer experience for young people is core to their work and that they are reviewing the claims.

This legal action follows similar lawsuits, including one by four US states against Meta and a settlement by Meta, Snap, and TikTok with a Kentucky school district over social media addiction.
